claims.text: Single-phase ZrB2 conventionally requires sintering above 2300 °C to achieve sufficient densification.
The proposed intervention is incorporation of approximately 5–10 vol% SiC into ZrB2 powder before sintering.
Adding 5–10 vol% SiC permits ZrB2 densification at temperatures below 2300 °C.
The proposed SiC-containing material can be sintered in the 2000–2200 °C range under inert atmosphere or vacuum.
SiC induces a transient liquid phase at ZrB2 grain boundaries during sintering.
The proposed transient liquid phase accelerates mass transport.
The proposed transient liquid phase promotes particle rearrangement and grain-boundary diffusion.
Accelerated mass transport increases densification and reduces the residual pore network.
Residual pores provide penetration pathways for a liquid plating bath.
Reducing the number or size of pores will reduce hole formation during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
Reducing hole formation will lower the likelihood of eventual component failure.
SiC-containing ZrB2 sintered at 2000–2200 °C is predicted to have significantly lower porosity than pure ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
SiC-containing ZrB2 sintered at 2000–2200 °C is predicted to have mechanical integrity similar or superior to pure ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C.
SiC-containing ZrB2 is predicted to resist degradation in a liquid plating bath better than conventionally sintered pure ZrB2.
Conventionally prepared pure ZrB2 has greater residual porosity and a greater likelihood of plating-bath-induced hole formation than the proposed SiC-containing material.
The proposed service boundary is exposure for approximately 6–24 hours to a liquid plating bath representative of industrial composition and temperature.
